summaries.sum-13-cider-press: The Dunmere cider press, an 1850s oak screw press, has been restored by volunteers using seasoned oak and a hand-cut thread, and will press apples again this autumn after forty years.
summaries.sum-14-quarry-lake: Swimming is allowed at Ketley quarry lake for the first time this summer, with lifeguards on duty 10–6, June–September. A roped shallow area and buoyed course exist; entry is free after registering, parking limited to sixty cars.
summaries.sum-15-bookbinder: Marisa Venn, the county's last bookbinder, has taken her first apprentice, who will train two years in hand techniques before serving customers; a heritage crafts grant helps fund it.
summaries.sum-16-cliff-path: A landslip has closed the coast path at Gannet Head, removing twenty metres of cliff edge; walkers detour inland via a farm track. Authorities will survey later and build a new path further inland.
summaries.sum-17-clockmaker: The Holloway town clock, mounted above the market hall since 1911 and losing a minute daily from a worn bearing and bent pendulum rod, has stopped for six weeks while new parts are made and its faces cleaned.
summaries.sum-18-heron-rookery: Wimble Carr's heronry recorded forty-one nests this spring, a record since 1962, as herons nest in alders; mild weather and a shooting ban likely helped.
summaries.sum-29-brindle-viaduct: Brindle Viaduct strengthening was rebudgeted from eighteen months and £2.4m to nine months and £3.1m, using a steel deck, four weekend closures from October, plus replacement buses.
summaries.sum-30-ganister-tarn: Ganister Tarn's upper path remains open, contrary to online claims; only the north car park–boathouse link closed 1 September for bank stabilisation, reopening before Christmas. Boots advised.
summaries.sum-31-quernmore-kiln: A survey of the Quernmore bottle kiln, leaning 340mm out of plumb, urges rebuilding its top two metres; £190,000 needed, £55,000 held. No firing planned.
summaries.sum-32-hessle-mills: Hessle Low Mill, a tower mill, wins £74,000 for cap and sails; Hessle High Mill, a smock mill, was refused as too dilapidated and must resubmit. Both listed.
summaries.sum-33-cotterdale-bus: From November the Cotterdale–Hawes 831 bus runs Saturdays only, with four return journeys unchanged; the unsubsidised Tuesday service becomes a demand-responsive minibus trial.
summaries.sum-34-alder-carr: Alder Carr's 2026 survey found 46 willow tit pairs, a record high up from 31 in 2023, credited to four hectares of new wet woodland and a mild spring.
summaries.sum-35-priory-gatehouse: Twelve weeks of stonework, repointing and lead roof renewal begin at the Priory gatehouse in February; it stays open except two April weeks. Precinct wall assessed later.
summaries.sum-36-larkfield-quarry: The Larkfield quarry extension was approved Tuesday, conditional on a bat survey and a widened Pitt Lane access road; lorries are capped at 48 daily, none before 07:00. Objectors sought refusal over noise.
summaries.sum-37-ryhope-pool: Ryhope pool, due to reopen on 3 June, opened 19 August after its new plant room flooded and a pump came from Italy. Weekday opening is now 06:30; diving boards await inspection.
summaries.sum-38-bewick-refusals: Bewick's licence refusal rate fell from 9 to 6 per cent, but refusals rose from 41 to 58 as applications nearly doubled. Nine of 14 appeals succeeded; officers credit the new late-night levy exemption.
summaries.sum-39-coldbeck-society: The Coldbeck Co-operative Society has purchased the former auction mart at Stang Bridge, rather than the Coldbeck Foot mill it had pursued since 2023, and will create a food store and eleven flats. The mill remains unsold.
summaries.sum-46-thwaite-lane-bridge: A 7.5-tonne weight limit took effect Monday on the Thwaite Lane bridge after cracking was found in the eastern abutment. The council's assessment will take six weeks and may lift the limit; buses are diverted through Sowerby, adding eleven minutes.
summaries.sum-47-eller-beck-hatchery: A parasite in two holding tanks halted this year's stocking from the Eller Beck hatchery. The tanks were disinfected, stocking resumes next season, and upstream angling clubs are unaffected.
summaries.sum-48-marsden-gate-quarry: Blasting at Marsden Gate quarry has been suspended since an August complaint of cracked plaster at a Fold Lane house, though the operator's monitors showed vibration within limits. Crushing and haulage continue, with lorry movements steady at sixty daily.
summaries.sum-49-birkrigg-allotments: Birkrigg allotments will convert twenty-two of ninety plots into a community orchard, agreed by the association's committee in September. The council, the landowner, says no planning permission is required; eleven waiting-list applicants were offered the southern terrace instead.
